## 0. Executive Synthesis (read this first)

The corpus splits into **three architectural tribes**, and the winning design is a deliberate hybrid that takes one specific thing from each:

| Tribe | Members | What they nail | What they get wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Session managers** | agent-of-empires, orca, paseo, agent-orchestrator | worktree lifecycle, PTY/harness wrapping, multi-surface (TUI/web/mobile) | daemon owns all truth → single point of failure; worktree-per-agent disk explosion |
| **Coordination protocols / gates** | opencode-swarm, agent-swarm | gated review pipelines, scope enforcement, write detection | LLM-heavy coordination burns the token budget the work was supposed to spend |
| **Runtimes & learning** | oh-my-pi, claude-smart, munder-difflin, iPolloWork, Orkas | tool/IDE depth, durable skill learning, multi-runtime pluggability | weak isolation; context growth is the failure mode |

### Four findings that change the plan

1. **Tool-schema bloat is now a measured number, not a feeling.** `agent-swarm` recorded **118 tools ≈ 311 KB ≈ 80K tokens → 8 script tools ≈ 8.8 KB ≈ 2.2K tokens (~35×)**, and noted that only Claude has ToolSearch — "pi/codex/opencode have no tool-search, so for them the full schema really does enter every session." `[VERIFIED thoughts/shared/research/2026-07-11-scripts-only-mcp-experiment.md]` Pillar 3 is the highest-ROI item in the whole product, and it is a *solved* problem waiting to be generalized.

2. **Progressive tool disclosure already exists in production** — `oh-my-pi`'s `xd://` virtual devices demote rarely-used tools out of the schema and expand them on demand (`ToolLoadMode essential|discoverable`). `[VERIFIED tools/xdev.ts]` Studio's Tool Lens should be a fleet-wide generalization of this, not an invention.

3. **The corpus's central failure mode is decorative orchestration.** iPolloWork declares a `dependency|parallel` graph and **never walks it**; agent-orchestrator has **no dependency concept at all**; Orkas **deleted** its plan DAG in favor of prompt-driven dispatch. Only `agent-swarm` has a real `dependsOn` queue — and it has zero referential integrity. `[VERIFIED §2]` A DAG that no deterministic scheduler executes is worse than no DAG.

4. **Nobody has solved write conflicts at the semantic layer.** Everyone ships worktrees and then a merge queue to undo the damage. The three primitives to do better exist separately in the ecosystem (`wit` function locks, `foremerge` write-intent, `Zaivern` line ownership) and in-repo (`opencode-swarm`'s scope leases + shell-write detection). **This is Studio's defensible gap.**

**The thesis this document argues:** Studio should not be "another daemon with worktrees and a dashboard." Its defensible core is a **zero-token coordination plane** (deterministic, no model in the dispatch loop) over a **write-intent fabric** (semantic scope claims instead of default worktree cloning), with a **Tool Lens** MCP proxy (progressive schema disclosure + role capability manifests — the 35× lever), and a **session bridge that is literally ACP** — an existing open standard — rather than N bespoke adapters. The cockpit is a projection of that plane, not a second source of truth.

The three most falsifiable bets are stated as `[HYPOTHESIS]` in §4.3 and should be spiked before any of the rest of the roadmap is committed.

## 2. Phase 1 — Forensic Codebase Audit Matrix

> Grounded in four parallel source-level audits of the corpus. Evidence markers are `[VERIFIED path]`; where a claim rests on a README rather than source, it is marked `[INFERRED: README]`.

### 2.1 — 2.12 Repository Inventory Matrix

#### iPolloWork — engine-neutral workbench
**Philosophy:** One plugin-package platform + project-workspace model projected onto every agent runtime (OpenCode / DeepSeek Harness / Codex), so one install inventory serves present and future engines. `[VERIFIED review/iPolloWork/specs/plugin-platform-architecture.md]`

**Orchestration model:** Project-config-driven, **not** chat-driven. `ProjectWorkspaceConfig` declares a goal, up to 24 named agents, and an `orchestration` graph of `entryAgentId` + `relations` typed `dependency | parallel` `[VERIFIED packages/types/src/project-workspace.ts:88-110]`. Agents pin `role`, `prompt`, `skillIds`, `pluginIds`, and a `runtime` (engineId/model/mode) `[VERIFIED :65-87]`. Execution freezes `projectRevision` + agent + runtime into `execution_json` `[VERIFIED apps/server/src/work-items.ts:648-690]`. Scheduling = work-item automations (`once|daily|weekly`) claimed via a SQLite lease (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` + `automation_lease_until`) with a `runKey` anti-idempotency token in the prompt `[VERIFIED apps/server/src/work-items.ts:840-910]`.
**Critical finding — the DAG is decorative.** `relations: dependency|parallel` is validated and drawn in `domains/work/project-orchestration-graph.tsx`, but **no runtime walks it**. Decomposition quality depends entirely on the entry agent's prose prompt.

**Plugin/Skill/role registry:** Manifest schema v2 in `packages/types/src/plugins.ts`. Resource kinds: `skill|agent|command|tool|mcp|provider|hook|context|secret|file|local-service|native-binary|ui`; permissions: `network, workspace-read, workspace-write, process, clipboard, notifications, camera, microphone, geolocation` `[VERIFIED plugins.ts:46-62]`. Resources declare `requires`/`provides` relation strings with install-time referential integrity `[VERIFIED plugins.ts:560-640]`. Auth: `secret-form | oauth-pkce | device-code | hosted-browser`.
**Critical finding — role scoping is prose.** `skillIds`/`pluginIds` are only rendered into the system prompt ("Assigned plugins: …") `[VERIFIED packages/types/src/work-items.ts:109-127]`. Nothing filters the engine's tool/skill surface per agent. Context flooding and cross-role leakage are structural.

**Multi-runtime bridge:** `PluginEngineAdapter` (`compatibility()`, `workspaceFiles()`, `skillTargetPath()`, `syncRuntime()`) with three adapters and an explicit `ready | partial | unsupported` compatibility matrix instead of silent divergence `[VERIFIED apps/server/src/plugin-engine-adapter.ts:46-128]`. Uniform host capabilities reach every engine via **one loopback MCP endpoint** (`engineHostMcp`) exposing 14 host tools, including a full ref-based browser control surface and a consequential-control regex that forces approval `[VERIFIED apps/server/src/engine-host-tools.ts:1-90]`. Engine processes: OpenCode spawned managed; Codex/DSH as stdio JSON-RPC CLIs; histories normalized into a shared `session-read-model.ts`.

**Persistence:** Per-workspace SQLite work-items with versioned optimistic concurrency (`expectedVersion`) + automation lease; engine-neutral state in `runtime.sqlite`; `SessionArtifact` with generation metadata and `previousPaths` for renames.

**Standout innovations:**
- Portable package + engine projection split with an honest compatibility matrix — `plugin-engine-adapter.ts:46-128`
- Host MCP tool plane as the engine-agnostic API — `engine-host-mcp.ts` + `engine-host-tools.ts`
- `requires`/`provides` relation graph with install-time referential integrity — `packages/types/src/plugins.ts:560-640`
- Capability-bound plugin authorization (a local service cannot address another installation) — `plugin-platform-runtime.ts:37-53`
- Lease-based scheduled execution + `runKey` idempotency + schedule preview→confirm→apply two-phase import — `work-items.ts:840-960`, `routes/core.ts:383-470`

**Major flaws:**
- Agent skill/plugin scoping is **prompt text, not enforcement** — `work-items.ts:109-127`
- Orchestration graph is **decorative** — declared, drawn, never executed — `project-workspace.ts:88-110`
- No cross-engine project sessions; `projectApply` hard-fails on engine mismatch — `routes/core.ts:355-363`
- Engine-native plugins share the engine process — no hard isolation (spec concedes this)
- Policy-as-prompt blobs: enormous imperative strings as a contract surface — `engine-host-tools.ts:38-80`
- Project-builder gating is an in-memory `Set` that vanishes on restart — `routes/core.ts:310-316`

#### Orkas — commander-in-the-loop group chat
**Philosophy:** One routing-first orchestrator either handles work itself or hands it to named specialists with isolated skills, memory, and tool groups.

**Orchestration model:** Explicitly **not** a plan DAG — `plan_executor.ts:1-16` records that "G8b replaced static plans with the commander-in-the-loop model". Three routing tools `[VERIFIED src/main/features/group_chat/bus.ts:8761-9010]`:
- `hand_off_to` — terminal delegation; ends the commander turn
- `dispatch_to` — non-terminal, synchronous, **parallel-safe** (`executionMode: 'parallel'`); returns the worker's result for synthesis
- `run_worker` — anonymous isolated helper, no history, no named-agent skills

Sequencing/parallelism/recovery are **LLM decisions** constrained only by prompt text and host budgets (`COMMANDER_MAX_TOOL_LOOPS = 120`, `AGENT_MAX_TOOL_LOOPS = 100` in `actor-budgets.ts`). Cross-message ordering: "one message's written order IS its execution order by default". A host-driven task board tracks `queued|running|waiting_input|blocked|done|stopped|failed|cancelled` — **"The model has no board-writing tool"** `[VERIFIED task_board.ts:1-35]`.

**Plugin/Skill/role registry:** One `agent.json` per agent (`workflow` markdown, `skill_list`, `tool_list`, declarative `inputs`, `output_format`, `runtime` backend). **The anti-context-flooding core is the tool catalog**: hierarchical `ToolGroupId`s (`workspace.read/write/execute`, `office.*`, `media.*`, `connectors`, `context`, `orchestration`, `management.*`, `runtime`) with per-entry `loadGroups`, `ownerAgent` isolation, `agentAssignable`, `permission: 'localExec'`, and `programmatic` policies for nested `run_program` `[VERIFIED src/main/model/core-agent/tool-catalog.ts:11-237]`. Commander activates groups via `tool_load`; **"loading never grants" permission**. An agent's `tool_list` is a hard cap — "The Agent cannot load groups beyond this list" — with a lowest-privilege fallback set. Skills use source tiers `builtin > platform > custom > external > global` with per-agent allowlists and a roster token budget `SKILL_DESCRIPTION_ROSTER_MAX_TOKENS`.

**Multi-runtime bridge:** In-process `core-agent` runner, plus `AgentRuntime.kind === 'cli'` spawning external CLIs behind a **`LocalCliCapabilities` contract**: `resume: 'native'|'session-id'|'none'`, `instructionChannel: 'native'|'user-message'`, `durableInstructionScope`, `codingProjectDirectory`, `agentMemory`, `activeRunIngress: 'codex-app-server'|'stream-json'|'none'`, and `LocalCliPermissionPolicy: 'inherit'|'ask'|'full_access'` `[VERIFIED src/main/features/local_agents/registry.ts:37-80]`. Backends: `backends/{claude,codex,opencode,hermes,openclaw}.ts` + ACP diagnostics.

**Persistence:** Entirely file-based per-uid tree: JSONL conversation sessions, group-chat `members.json`/`state.json`/`plan.json`, `tasks.json` board snapshots ("atomic whole-file snapshot… deliberately NOT inside state.json"), per-agent `MEMORY.md`, project `ORKAS.md`, `runtime_stats.json` kept **outside** `agent.json` so definitions aren't rewritten per dispatch. Vector KB at `vector.db`.

**Standout innovations:**
- Three-way delegation contract (terminal / consume-and-synthesize / anonymous) with parallel-safe dispatch — `bus.ts:8761-9010`
- Tool-group catalog + `tool_load` lazy activation, `ownerAgent` isolation, Commander-only tools — `tool-catalog.ts` ← **closest existing ancestor of our FV3 Tool Lens**
- `LocalCliCapabilities` resume/instruction/ingress contract — cleanest multi-CLI harness abstraction in the corpus — `local_agents/registry.ts:37-80`
- Host-owned task board the model cannot write — `task_board.ts:1-35`
- Self-evolution split (COMPETENCE.md vs LEARNING_STRATEGIES.md) with an explicit untrusted-evidence boundary — `core-agent/src/evolution/metacognition.ts:8-60`
- Per-role tool-loop budgets in a tiny auditable module — `actor-budgets.ts`

**Major flaws:**
- God modules: `bus.ts` is 10,751 lines; `video-studio-tool.ts` 12,410; `local-tools.ts` 6,313
- Skill scoping is **explicitly not an authorization boundary** — `bus.ts:5351-5353` says so
- **No deterministic orchestration**: the plan DAG was deleted; no machine-checkable plan to resume or audit — `plan_executor.ts:5-13`
- Hard-coded opaque agent IDs couple the catalog to marketplace identity — `tool-catalog.ts:74-79`
- Schedules silently skip missed windows — `auto_tasks.ts:22-23` (wrong for unattended work)

#### awesome-agent-orchestrators — ecosystem pattern catalog
**Taxonomy:** organizes by **human supervision modality**, not architecture (Terminal parallel · Desktop/Web parallel · Multi-Agent Swarms · Autonomous Loop Runners · Autonomous Task Runners · Agent Infrastructure & Primitives · Personal Assistants · Resting). Implicit second axis: backend coverage (which CLI agents each drives) and license posture. Treat the taxonomy as go-to-market framing; the **per-entry blurbs are the pattern source**.

**Named patterns worth adopting (verified in README):**
- **Durable mailbox / inter-agent messaging** as the coordination substrate (Cyclops FIFO-per-recipient; Concord MCP "claim work, detect edit collisions, transfer ownership"; Agent Messaging Protocol "Ed25519-signed envelopes"; `gnap` "git as a task board with no orchestrator process")
- **Hand-off vs dispatch vs ownership transfer** (GraphCode, `foremerge`)
- **Independent verification gates** (`kodo`, `no_human` "a second model in a fresh session… told to refute 'done'", `toryo` quality ratcheting)
- **Merge queues & collision control** (`gastown` Bors-style, `YYLO` risk-based + receipts, `Zaivern` line-level ownership, `wit` Tree-sitter function locks)
- **Runbook → SKILL.md compilation** (`agent-runbook`) and **skill lockfiles** (`skillfold`)
- **Replay/receipts** (`OrcaReplay` process+socket boundary → one timeline; `MartinLoop` run receipts; `aGiTrack` commit-per-turn with token cost)
- **Approval inbox** across agents (`Calyx`, `octomux`, `intentic` per-turn credential capabilities)
- **Quota-aware harness rotation** (`Claudexor`)
- **Org-chart metaphors as structure** (`5dive`, `multi-agent-shogun`, `paperclip`)

#### oh-my-pi — the agent runtime that already solved tool-schema flooding
**Philosophy:** "A coding agent with the IDE wired in" — cache- and token-obsessed runtime where every layer exists to squeeze more real work out of the context window. ~80k lines Rust core + TS/Bun, 31 built-in tools, 14 LSP ops, 28 DAP ops.

**Agent loop & context handling:** `AgentMessage` throughout; transforms to `Message[]` only at the LLM call boundary `[VERIFIED packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts]`. **Cache stabilization is two mechanisms** `[VERIFIED packages/agent/src/append-only-context.ts:1-25]`: `StablePrefix` (system prompt + tool specs frozen; `invalidate()` only on MCP reconnect) and `AppendOnlyLog` (messages only grow; prior turns never re-serialized) — so only the new user delta is a cache miss. Four compaction strategies (LLM summarization, mechanical pruning, surgical elision, image-archival) behind a structured `CompactionEntry` carrying `summary`, `firstKeptEntryId`, `tokensBefore`, `providerReplayThroughEntryId`, `preserveData` `[VERIFIED compaction/entries.ts:31-55]`. Native per-family Rust tokenizers (claude-v3/v47/v5, qwen3, deepseek-v3, kimi-k2, glm5), not char/4 estimates `[VERIFIED tokenizer.ts:13-27]`. `fitOutputTokensToContextWindow` sizes `maxTokens` from the provider's own last usage anchor + only the appended tail `[VERIFIED output-budget.ts:17-40]`.

**Tool registration/scoping — THE finding of this audit:**
`ToolLoadMode = "essential" | "discoverable"` `[VERIFIED packages/agent/src/types.ts:984-991]`, with `ESSENTIAL_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES` pinned so adapter re-registration can never demote a built-in `[VERIFIED tools/essential-tools.ts:23-46]`.
**`xd://` virtual tool devices** `[VERIFIED packages/coding-agent/src/tools/xdev.ts:1-31]`: discoverable tools are **unmounted from the request tools array** and exposed as `read xd://` (listing), `read xd://<tool>` (docs + JSON schema), `write xd://<tool>` (execute). One wire schema per tool, zero dispatcher duplication. `XDEV_KEEP_TOP_LEVEL` pins what must never mount (todo, yield, ask, grep, web_search).
**This is progressive tool disclosure, implemented and in production** — exactly the FV3 mechanism. It also ships `sent-tool-definitions.ts` to re-declare withdrawn tools byte-identically when a provider keeps stale tool declarations. Approval tiers `always-ask|write|yolo` with per-tool policy and deliberate non-inheritance of `allow` across renamed tools `[VERIFIED approval.ts:17-24]`.

**Skills/memory:** `LearnTool` persists a durable lesson AND mints a managed skill in one call `[VERIFIED tools/learn.ts:43-50]`. Pluggable memory backends (`hindsight`, `mnemopi` SQLite, `sharpshooter`, `local`, `off`). **`MemoryRow` carries a full statement-lifetime model**: `veracity` (stated|inferred|tool|imported|unknown), `valid_until`, `superseded_by`, `trust_tier`, `recall_count` `[VERIFIED packages/mnemopi/src/types.ts:9-28]`. Retrieval runs four "voices" (vector/graph/fact/temporal) scored into `combined_score` `[VERIFIED polyphonic-recall.ts:8-33]`. Skill descriptions are LLM-compressed to 160 chars/12 words on a `Semaphore(4)` to keep the listing cheap `[VERIFIED extensibility/skill-descriptions.ts:16-25]`. Context notes hard-capped at 16,384 bytes.

**Persistence & accounting:** tiered session storage (SQL/Redis/indexed/foreign JSONL + `claude-session-store`/`codex-session-store`). Compaction accounting is first-class: `tokensBefore` on every entry, `ShakeResult.tokensFreed`. `packages/stats/` aggregates usage windows and compaction savings.

**Standout innovations:**
- **`xd://` discoverable tool mounting** — `tools/xdev.ts` + `types.ts:984-1091`. The single best answer to tool-schema context flooding in the entire corpus.
- **`append-only-context.ts` StablePrefix/AppendOnlyLog** — cleanest cache-prefix stabilization seen anywhere.
- **Compaction protection matchers** — never prune `skill://` reads or `artifact://` recovery reads (eliding an artifact recovery "mints another artifact and can repeat indefinitely") `[VERIFIED compaction/tool-protection.ts:38-50]`
- **Snapcompact** — archive discarded history as PNG frames of pixel-font text that vision models read back; eval-backed per-provider frame shapes (f1 .351–.934). Even without shipping image compaction, the *eval-backed shape table method* is worth copying.
- **lspmux** — shared language-server instances across windows + diagnostics ledger.
- **`fitOutputTokensToContextWindow`** with provider-usage anchor.

**Major flaws:**
- Snapcompact fidelity is provider-brittle (f1 .351 below OCR floor) — compaction quality coupled to vision-encoder quirks.
- The `xd://` demotion footgun recurs: re-registering a built-in "would silently demote it to discoverable and unmount it" (issue #5764); hiding `read`/`write` "leaves every mounted device unreachable" — two issue numbers for one bug class.
- Session module sprawl: `session/` holds 80+ files, `agent-session.ts` past 3800 lines.
- Compaction state machine is a race nursery (compaction interleaving with live turns, provider replays, message-cache invalidation) — guarded, not owned.
- Skill-description compression is an unbounded background LLM tax.

#### claude-smart — durable skill learning via a host-CLI LLM loop
**Philosophy:** Thin multi-host hook shell that buffers interactions and delegates learning to an external `reflexio` engine (LLM extraction over sliding windows), injecting query-matched skills back as just-in-time `additionalContext`. Never crashes the host session; learning rides the host CLI so it is keyless.

**Agent loop & context handling:** Six lifecycle hooks (Setup/SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd) through `hook_entry.sh`. **PreToolUse is scoped to `Edit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash`** `[VERIFIED plugin/hooks/hooks.json:54-56]`. Handlers swallow all exceptions — "hooks must never crash the session" `[VERIFIED hook.py:173]`. SessionStart deliberately does **not** retrieve memory; retrieval is just-in-time on prompts and mutating tool calls. Extraction cadence `window_size=5, stride_size=3`. The extraction LLM **is the host CLI** (`claude -p` / `codex exec` / `opencode run`) via compat bridges.

**Tool registration/scoping:** registers no tools — it observes host tools via hook matchers. A shared injection pipeline (search → render → persist citation registry → emit `additionalContext`) is identical for PreToolUse and UserPromptSubmit `[VERIFIED context_inject.py:28-97]`.

**Skills/memory:** Three entity types — `profiles`, `user_playbooks`, `agent_playbooks`. Retrieval is one hybrid (BM25+vector RRF) round trip with **server-side per-session dedup** (each rule injects once per session, next-best backfill) `[VERIFIED reflexio_adapter.py:440-495]`. Injection bullets carry rank+fingerprint citation ids with a **counterfactual cite-bar** ("your answer would be substantively different if the item had not been shown") resolved at Stop against a per-session registry.

**Standout innovations:**
- **Idempotent publish batching** — `publish_attempt {start,end}` freeze markers + deterministic `uuid5(session_id, start, end)` request ids so a duplicated drain is server-side idempotent `[VERIFIED publish.py:20-61]`. Best concurrency design in the repo.
- **Citation/attribution protocol** closing "was this memory actually used?" — `cs_cite.py:228-261` + `state.py:146-209`
- **Host-CLI-as-LLM-provider bridges** (`codex-claude-compat.js`, `opencode-claude-compat.js`) — keyless learning on any host
- **Self-feedback/recursion guard** with layered signals (env marker, non-interactive entrypoint, cwd-inside-checkout, prompt-shape fingerprints) `[VERIFIED internal_call.py:83-113]`
- **Wire-field allowlist with written rationale** — `created_at` deliberately not sent because backdated batches fall behind the extractor bookmark and become "permanent, silent loss of learning data"

**Major flaws (a cautionary tale for Studio):**
- **Token leak in injected context** — no budget: full `content`+`trigger`+`rationale` verbatim plus a ~150–250 token citation instruction re-appended on **every** injection, and PreToolUse fires on every Edit/Write/Bash. A busy session pays that fixed tax dozens of times. `ARCHITECTURE.md` admits compacted sessions never re-inject rules that fell out of context while still re-paying the instruction.
- Unbounded local buffer growth + O(n) re-reads on every Stop.
- Brittle string-marker parsing as a core data path (plan decisions match hardcoded English phrases; handlers swallow everything).
- Race windows: unbounded `while True` retry with no backoff; read-then-append TOCTOU.
- The most important logic lives outside the repo (`reflexio-ai`).

#### munder-difflin — the Hive: filesystem coordination under a god-orchestrator
**Philosophy:** "Office of your clones" — drive subscription coding CLIs as PTY-spawned interactive agents (**never the Agent SDK**, to stay on interactive plan quota) coordinating through a filesystem hive of mailboxes + blackboard + single-committer git, rendered as avatars on a Pixi office floor.

**Agent loop & context handling:** Real interactive TUI via `node-pty` `[VERIFIED src/main/pty.ts:331-552]`. Session state survives respawn (`sessionId` spread before spawn meta). **Two-channel, cache-aware context injection:** system-prompt prefix via `--append-system-prompt` carries a documented **prompt-cache invariant** — "keep this prefix VOLATILE-FREE … Do NOT add dates, UUIDs, counters, board/registry state" `[VERIFIED src/main/hive.ts:1412-1418]` — while volatile context (live roster with `ctx NN%` occupancy, standing goal, operator steer notes) rides `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` `[VERIFIED hooks.ts:289-348]`. The Stop-hook autonomous loop is **retired** ("Never turn unread hive mail into a forced continuation at Stop").

**Tool registration/scoping:** The harness registers no agent tools — it *scopes* what the wrapped CLI can do:
- PreToolUse deny gate with race-free immediate `permissionDecision: 'deny'` (no renderer round-trip) `[VERIFIED hooks.ts:270-287]`
- Sandbox writable roots per agent
- MCP catalog with tiers: `safe-readonly` auto-enables; write/secret tiers surface as `consentRequired` and are never auto-enabled
- **Default-deny flag allowlist** `SAFE_FLAG_NAMES = {--model, --max-turns, --output-format, --verbose}` for untrusted hire manifests, after **three documented prior escapes** (`-c model_providers.*.base_url`, `--provider`, codex `-a`/`-s`) `[VERIFIED src/shared/hire.ts:100-131]`
- Voice action tiering with distinct-token verbal confirm ("NEVER a bare `yes`, so ambient speech can't authorize a kill")

**Multi-agent coordination — The Hive** `[VERIFIED src/main/hive.ts:1-20]`: one git repo holding `registry.json`, `board.md` (god is sole scribe), `tasks.json`, `log.jsonl`, and `agents/<id>/{identity.md, memory.md, inbox/, outbox/}`. Two locked rules: **single committer** (agents never call git) and **single-writer-per-file**.
- **Speech-act message schema** `[VERIFIED hive.ts:54-67]`: `MessageAct = request|inform|propose|query|agree|refuse|done` with `in_reply_to`, `requires_reply`, `needs_human`. PROTOCOL.md teaches: "`inform` and `done` are terminal — don't reply to them, or two agents will loop forever."
- **Delivery tiers with loud failure** `[VERIFIED hive.ts:1556-1646]`: inbox-file / terminal-handoff / synthesized-proxy-event / **bounce to god** with `[undeliverable — …]`. Log records `delivered` not intent, so a drop can never read as delivered.
- **Closing Time** graceful shutdown entirely over the message rails (broadcast → ACK → COMPLETE).
- Five-layer memory stack including MemoryReflector (backup-first → verify-don't-trust → atomic swap) and a quarantine reaper after a user hit **100GB in 8 hours** from an upstream never-delete bug.

**Persistence & accounting:** SQLite is a thin `kv` + `command_history` slice; heavy state is files + single-committer git (with `gc.autoDetach=false` after background gc caused ~3.5% ENOTEMPTY). **Cost accounting is a locked seam** (`UsageProvider.getAgentUsage` only) with a loopback OTel collector primary and a per-file incremental transcript offset cache that prices **each record by its own model**. `costLifetime.ts` recovers true lifetime spend across restart-reset counters by summing segment peaks — the last value had been hiding **59% of real spend**. Budget arms use `workTokensOf` (excludes cacheRead) vs display `tokensOf`.

**Standout innovations:**
- **`src/shared/taskLedger.ts:44-87`** — field-preserving merge so partial UI models cannot delete fields they don't know about ("silently DELETED every field it didn't know about, on EVERY card"). Best defensive-persistence pattern in the corpus.
- **Prompt-cache-stable injection rule** (stable prefix / volatile hook channel) — directly portable.
- **Proxy-bridge sidecar** — a loopback reverse proxy that observes a hookless CLI's LLM traffic and *synthesizes* hook payloads so unsupported CLIs get live status/cost/Stop semantics. Deliberate degradation is logged, never silent.
- **`costLifetime.ts` segment-peak fold** + `warm` so callers never publish a cold `$0` as fact.
- **Capability-token secret broker** — workers hold a per-worker handle; the broker injects the real credential upstream; the worker never sees it.
- **Untrusted-input hire manifest threat model** (`hire@1`) — complete small model for shareable agent configs.

**Major flaws (all verified in source):**
- **Synchronous `git add -A && git commit` on the Electron main thread, on every message.** `send()` → `commit()`; `spawnSync('git', …)` with 8s timeout `[VERIFIED hive.ts:1549-1553, 2683-2686]`. Same class of problem already produced a 7.5GB history.
- **`HOP_CAP` is a no-op loop guard** — `hops` is declared, defaulted to 0, checked against `HOP_CAP = 12`, and **never incremented anywhere** `[VERIFIED hive.ts:65, 1531, 1557]`. Request↔request ping-pong is unbounded.
- **`drainForStop` cursor bug and dead code** — advances past every fresh message before the agent acts; the renderer already switched to a Set for the same reason; the Stop path itself is retired.
- **At-least-once outbox delivery with a crash window** (deliver then rename); torn writes get quarantined and **dropped** with only a log line, no god-bounce.
- **PTY idle-settle heuristics will truncate real work** — 3.5s quiet = response-complete; any build/fetch with a longer gap ends capture. `STALE_INPUT_MS` 30 minutes blocks all queue delivery by design.

#### agent-of-empires — tmux-native session supervisor with lease/epoch hygiene
**Philosophy:** Every agent is a session (terminal *or* structured ACP) under one supervisor; worktrees and Docker sandboxes are first-class lifecycle objects.

**Orchestration model:** Supervisor-per-session over an epoch/lease lifecycle table — not actors or queues. "Owns each structured view session's worker, bridges its events into the broadcast sink, and respawns it on crash within a budget": `MAX_RESPAWNS_IN_WINDOW = 3`, `RESTART_WINDOW = 60s`, `RESPAWN_BACKOFF = 500ms` `[VERIFIED src/acp/supervisor/mod.rs:38-41]`. `WorkerHandle` carries `client`, `drain_task`, `restart_history`, `kind: Runner|Attached|Stdio`, and a `Lease` `[VERIFIED mod.rs:115-123]`. **`ResumeReservation` is an RAII guard whose `Drop` calls `lifecycle.abandon()`** so a failed resume cannot pin a session `[VERIFIED mod.rs:176-194]`. Admission enforces `max_concurrent_workers` against `table.occupied_slots() + registry_count` `[VERIFIED launch.rs:42-88]`. Epoch authority `Lease { epoch: u64 }` with `WorkerPhase::{Absent,Resuming,Running,Stopping}` and documented lock order "workers before lifecycle" `[VERIFIED runner_lifecycle.rs:29-48]`. `peer_pid_from_socket` caps connect at 100ms so a wedged runner cannot stall a caller.

**Worktree engine:** `create_worktree` runs fetch (10s timeout, stdin nulled to suppress passphrase prompts) → create branch → `add_worktree` → **`convert_git_file_to_relative`** (so a checkout resolves when mounted in a container) → submodules → `lock_worktree` `[VERIFIED src/git/worktree/create.rs:110-180]`. The lock is a deliberate **prune fence**: `WORKTREE_LOCK_REASON = "aoe-managed worktree (prevents cross-boundary prune)"` keeps a sibling sandbox's `git worktree prune` from reaping admin entries (#2414); unlock is idempotent and must precede intentional remove `[VERIFIED mod.rs:25-29, 172-200]`. All mutations bounded by `WORKTREE_MUTATION_TIMEOUT = 30s`. Cleanup refuses the main repo, prefers `remove_dir` over `remove_dir_all` (only under `force`), retries 5× with 250ms sleeps because "macOS Docker Desktop VirtioFS lags after a container removal"; `prune_empty_parent_dirs` climbs at most 4 hops and refuses home/root/ancestors `[VERIFIED src/git/cleanup.rs:29-132]`. Path drift reconciled as `Current | Moved(PathBuf) | Missing | Ambiguous(Vec<PathBuf>)`.

**Session harness:** Two coexisting. Terminal = tmux panes with **cross-process locks stored as tmux user options** (`@aoe_size_owner`, `@aoe_vt_owner`) with `VT_OWNER_TTL = 4s` / `SIZE_OWNER_HEARTBEAT = 1500ms` driven by atomic CAS — because `pipe-pane` is exclusive per pane `[VERIFIED src/tmux/session.rs:44-80]`. Structured = ACP subprocesses with `stored_acp_session_id` for `session/load`, `fork_from` for `session/fork`, `mcp_servers`, `sandbox_info`. **Three-tier env deny matrix** with distinct deny-reasons: blocks `PATH/HOME/USER/LANG/LC_ALL/TERM`, `AOE_TOKEN`, `LD_*`/`DYLD_*` ("dynamic linker hook, would alter child binary load"), pins `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, shared with the runner "so the policies cannot drift", plus `scrub_stderr_secrets` for `sk-*`/`ghp_*`/`AKIA*`/`Bearer` `[VERIFIED src/acp/acp_client/spawn.rs:70-118]`.

**Tool/MCP scoping:** `filter_for_capabilities` drops `http`/`sse` servers the agent did not advertise in `initialize` (stdio always kept) `[VERIFIED src/acp/mcp_config.rs:50-76]`. Plugins declare a capability taxonomy (`runtime.worker`, `session.read/write`, `process.spawn`, `net`, `fs.read/write`, …) with `TrustLevel::{Builtin, Community}` `[VERIFIED aoe-plugin-api/src/capability.rs:35-70]`.

**Persistence:** Protocol-agnostic SQLite event log — "opaque JSON keyed by topic and a caller-assigned `seq`" with `rate_limit_budgets`, and a prefix validated to `[a-z_]+` because "SQLite cannot bind identifiers" `[VERIFIED src/events/mod.rs:1-31]`. Write `Mutex<Connection>` + separate read-only `search_conn` with `query_only=ON`. `record()` appends (duplicate seq ignored), then `prune_retention` **exempting non-substantive event discriminants** (`AvailableCommandsUpdated`, `ModesAvailable`, …) `[VERIFIED src/acp/event_store/mod.rs:28-109]`. 33 versioned migrations.

**Major flaws:**
- tmux subsystem is ~22k lines of **screen scraping**; status detection strips ANSI and rule-matches pane text, so any agent UI restyle silently breaks state inference. Hook-vs-pane duality means agents without hooks *must* render a parseable pane shape — there is no third channel.
- `remove_worktree_dir` blocks with `thread::sleep` retries; its own comment admits an orphaned wrapper dir is "a cosmetic leak" — **disk hygiene is best-effort**.
- Concurrency accounting sums two sources of truth (`table.occupied_slots() + registry_count`) which can transiently disagree.
- Worktree prune protection is a **cooperation** protocol — a user `git worktree prune --force` still reaps admin entries.

**Cherry-pick:** `git worktree lock --reason` + unlock-before-remove protocol; env deny matrix with per-tier `denyreason` + stderr secret regex; event retention with substantive/non-substantive split + read-only search handle; bounded parent-dir pruning with home/root refusals; `WorktreePathResolution` reconcile.

#### orca — worktree lifecycle at industrial depth
**Philosophy:** Desktop orchestrator running agents side-by-side, each in its own worktree, with coordinator/worker orchestration and an execution-host abstraction spanning native/WSL/SSH.

**Orchestration model:** Coordinator state machine polling a SQLite orchestration DB, `phase: decomposing|dispatching|monitoring|merging|done`, `DEFAULT_POLL_MS = 2000`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_DEFAULT = 4` `[VERIFIED src/main/runtime/orchestration/coordinator.ts:27-113]`. Dispatch is a **single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction** that dedupes mutation receipts on `(caller_fingerprint, request_id, method, payload_hash)` and rejects a reused request id with different input as `request_mismatch` `[VERIFIED db/worker-dispatch/worker-dispatch-start.ts:48-78]`. Nesting capped at `NESTED_WORKER_MAX_DEPTH_DEFAULT = 1` with an **actionable refusal** ("Complete this task yourself") so a worker does not loop on a capability it will never get `[VERIFIED src/shared/nested-worker-depth.ts:6-19]`. Circuit breaking `DISPATCH_CIRCUIT_BREAK_FAILURES = 3`. Agent sessions are single-writer with an operation ledger and leases, plus orphan-child reaper and spawn-token process scan.

**Worktree engine:** ~140 worktree-specific modules. Creation is `git worktree add --detach --no-checkout` then `git reset --hard` — "reset materializes files without running user post-checkout hooks before submit" — then `lock`, all under `withRepoRefMaintenancePaused('worktree-prepare')` so a running idle pack's packed-refs lock cannot block the add `[VERIFIED src/main/git/worktree-create-preparation.ts:54-107]`. Failure → `git worktree remove --force --force` (double force for Git 2.25 locked removal). **The disk-hygiene breakthrough:** `git worktree remove` deletes multi-GB `node_modules` inside the remove IPC and "the UI sat on a spinner for 8-35s. Renaming the directory into a sibling trash root is a metadata operation, and the recursive delete then runs after the IPC has already returned." Entries `.orca-worktree-trash/wt-<epoch-ms>-<nonce>`, `TRASH_SWEEP_MAX_CONTAINERS = 200`, symlink/non-directory refusals `[VERIFIED src/main/worktree-trash.ts:1-55]`. Plus `worktree-removal-home-guard.ts`, `worktree-orphan-gitdir-proof.ts`, `local-orphaned-worktree-cleanup.ts`, `worktree-lineage-pruning.ts`.

**Session harness:** PTY-first (bun-pty flow control, suspension, Windows job objects, foreground-process-tracker). Claude driven through the Claude Agent SDK with dedicated spawn/queue/journal modules. **Launch sequencing inversion** — create the worktree *without* a startup agent, ask the execution host whether it can host a session for the now-resolved workspace, then build the surface: "A refusal becomes a terminal agent in the worktree just created, never a failed launch" `[VERIFIED src/main/agent-launch/agent-launch-executor.ts:9-15]`. PTY write settlement distinguishes `writeRefused('provider_cannot_settle')` from `writeUnverifiable('provider_threw_after_handoff')` because "a partial write that then threw cannot prove the transport took nothing" `[VERIFIED mailbox-pointer-pty-write.ts:13-27]`. Trust gating pre-writes the trust artifacts each CLI reads at startup (`~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/.workspace-trusted`, etc.) with bundle-version citations.

**Tool/MCP scoping:** Skills discovered/bundled/shared; `agent-skill-selection.ts` indexes only requested selectors because "a share request carries at most 512 of them while discovery can return every skill on the machine." Agent status is a **single store by policy** (enforced via AGENTS.md): "the execution host owns agent status in one store… new producers write into that store, and readers keep only presentation policy."

**Persistence:** Orchestration DB holds tasks, dispatch_contexts, worker_dispatches, coordinator_runs, decision_gates, mutation_receipts, mailboxes/messages, question threads, federation relay — migrations v2–v42. Task `status` computed at insert via `json_each` dependency check in SQL. Usage accounting scans provider JSONL in worker threads with incremental line offsets.

**Major flaws:**
- **Four+ parallel agent-launch paths** (documented in the module itself): orchestration dispatch, mobile create, CLI create, desktop tab each start agents their own way — "every launch-relevant change is a multi-site edit with drift risk."
- Coordinator is a **2-second poll loop**, not event-driven — bounded dispatch latency and constant wakeups.
- Extreme fragmentation: `runtime/orchestration/db/` 100+ files, `src/main/git/` ~140, including single-constant modules.
- Terminal scraping + bracketed-paste injection remain load-bearing; AGENTS.md mandates transcript-capture-based rules "because remembered screens were wrong."
- Execution-host matrix (native/WSL/SSH/relay + Windows job objects) multiplies every change.

**Cherry-pick:** trash-rename deferred deletion with nonce-scoped entries + bounded sweep; mutation-receipt dedupe schema; nested depth gate with actionable refusal strings; `--detach --no-checkout` → `reset --hard` → `lock` creation; PTY write settlement contract; `withRepoRefMaintenancePaused`; single status-store policy.

#### paseo — provider abstraction and plugin extensibility
**Philosophy:** Self-hosted local daemon owning your agents and dev environment, reachable from desktop/mobile/web/CLI, extensible by trusted TypeScript plugins; no telemetry, no forced log-ins.

**Orchestration model:** Process supervisor over one daemon worker + central agent manager with per-agent run-state machines. Supervisor forks the worker with `WORKER_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 1_000`, `WORKER_TERMINATION_GRACE_MS = 10_000`, exchanging typed `paseo:shutdown|ready|restart` lifecycle messages plus heartbeats `[VERIFIED packages/server/scripts/supervisor.ts:1-30]`. `agent-manager.ts` (5,363 lines) owns `ManagedAgent` lifecycle, `AgentRunState` (`ForegroundTurnWaiter`, `PendingForegroundRun`), `AgentStreamCoalescer`, `ProviderSubagentStore`.

**Worktree engine:** `createWorktreeCore` wraps creation in `runWithGitCommandPriority("high", …)` and resolves a **creation intent** covering `branch-off | checkout-branch | checkout-change-request | checkout-github-pr` with mnemonic-id slugs `[VERIFIED src/server/worktree-core.ts:45-125]`. Read paths set `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS: "0"`. Setup scripts get `PASEO_SOURCE_CHECKOUT_PATH` / `PASEO_WORKTREE_PATH` / `PASEO_BRANCH_NAME` / `PASEO_WORKTREE_PORT` and `cleanupOnFailure → rmSync(recursive, force)`. Deletion handles the half-removed case explicitly ("git worktree remove fails if the admin dir is already gone") then falls back to `git worktree prune` with 30s timeout `[VERIFIED utils/worktree.ts:1135-1148]`. Auto-archive on merge + workspace reconciliation live in `src/server/auto-archive-on-merge/`.

**Session harness:** One harness per provider protocol, all over stdio. Claude = official Agent SDK, "the raw SDK query import in this module only" so "Windows .cmd/.bat handling cannot diverge from the daemon path" `[VERIFIED providers/claude/query.ts:1-80]`. Codex = JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout with `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 14 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (**14 days**), 2s graceful/1s force shutdown, 8KB stderr cap. Generic JSONL-RPC harness with `JsonlFrameDecoder`, `JSONL_RPC_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`, `JSONL_RPC_NO_TIMEOUT` for LLM-backed blocking calls. OpenCode = HTTP server. Copilot/Cursor/Kimi/Kiro = `generic-acp-agent.ts` (ACP client with capability negotiation).

**Tool/MCP scoping:** Host tools exposed as an MCP server wrapping `createPaseoToolCatalog` with `addModelVisibleStructuredContent` to keep model-visible content separate from UI content `[VERIFIED server/agent/mcp-server.ts:33-52]`. Injection via `withRuntimePaseoMcpServer`: internal `paseo` HTTP server at `/mcp/agents?callerAgentId=<id>` with a `Bearer` capability token — "the daemon password is gated off this route, so without this header the agent's MCP requests are rejected" `[VERIFIED runtime-mcp-config.ts:30-56]`. Policy is flat per-provider `disabledTools` string list. Plugins run as forked children (`globalThis.eval` of the compiled bundle) with 30s request timeouts and log caps.

**Persistence:** Per-agent atomic JSON records with a serialized mutation queue; `STORED_AGENT_SCHEMA` holds config + `toolPolicy.preapproved` MCP entries + `persistence` handle `{provider, sessionId, nativeHandle, metadata}`; `beginDelete`/`remove` wait on pending writes `[VERIFIED agent-storage.ts:11-232]`. Timeline rows keyed by `epoch` + monotonic `seq`, fetch limit 200.

**Standout — the three-layer anti-context-flood stack:** `AGENT_STREAM_COALESCE_DEFAULT_WINDOW_MS = 60` batching → `TOOL_CALL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH = 64KB` truncation → `MAX_TOOL_INPUT_CHARS = 400` / `MAX_TOOL_SUMMARY_CHARS = 200` activity curation `[VERIFIED agent-stream-coalescer.ts, agent-timeline-content.ts:5-13, activity-curator.ts:6-7]`.

**Standout — plugin hygiene:** Zod-validated before-hooks with typed lifecycle event catalog; **static import-graph boundary enforcement** (`boundaries.test.ts` walks the TS import graph and fails on cross-runtime imports — server code cannot import client modules) `[VERIFIED packages/plugin/src/boundaries.test.ts]`.

**Major flaws:**
- `agent-manager.ts` is a 5,363-line god object (plus an 11k-line test file).
- Plugins are `globalThis.eval`'d in a forked child — process isolation protects the daemon from crashes but grants full machine access; the README's "install only code you trust" is the only gate. **Unlike AOE there is no capability taxonomy or trust level.**
- Codex transport default timeout is 14 days — a hung RPC holds a pending request and its timer for two weeks.
- Timeline durability rests on an in-memory store; `migrations/` has a single backfill (vs AOE's 33, orca's v2–v42).
- Tool policy is a flat `disabledTools` string list — no per-workspace, per-agent, or capability-class scoping.
- No nested-dispatch depth control; subagent proliferation bounded only by each provider's own limits.

**Cherry-pick:** zod-validated plugin before-hooks + typed lifecycle catalog; import-graph boundary test for SDK packages; capability-token MCP injection with per-agent attribution; **layered context-flood stack**; worktree creation intent enum; per-agent atomic JSON record store with serialized mutation queue; supervisor lifecycle IPC.

#### agent-orchestrator (AO) — derived-never-persisted state
**Philosophy:** Every coding task gets its own agent, workspace, and feedback loop; the Kanban is a *derived* operational view of session/PR/CI/review facts, never stored state.

**Orchestration model:** **No task graph and no scheduler.** Orchestration is direct spawn-delegation: an orchestrator session (or a human) creates one worker per task. `DelegateTask` calls `manager.Spawn` with `Kind: domain.KindWorker` then fires background title refinement `[VERIFIED backend/internal/service/session/delegation.go:67-114]`. Session kinds are only `worker` and `orchestrator`. **Liveness is fact-derivation, not heartbeats**: `DeriveStatus` emits `StatusNoSignal` when no hook has reported within a grace period (~90s) `[VERIFIED backend/pkg/contract/status.go:101-102]`. There is **no dependency-edge concept anywhere in `domain/`** — nothing to deadlock on. Board placement computed by `derivePRKanbanColumn` with a deterministic anti-flicker total order (column priority → `UpdatedAt` → URL); columns are "derived… never a persisted status" `[VERIFIED domain/kanban.go:22-25, contract/kanban.go:90-167]`.

**Role/tool scoping:** Roles are harness-shaped, not tool-shaped. The real least-privilege surface is the **review gateway**: reviewers get an AO-owned runtime dir with **the source checkout intentionally absent**, plus an immutable **content-addressed authorization manifest** for "one worker and an exact set of review runs"; `PrepareEnvironment` "never creates files in the project checkout"; owner-only `chmod 0700` `[VERIFIED backend/internal/reviewgateway/gateway.go:29-102, 227]`. Explicitly documented as *not* a sandbox: "limits where the CLI stores its own files but intentionally does not claim process, filesystem, or network containment."

**Worktree/branch isolation:** `branch+worktree` provisioning with `rollbackPreparedAdd` on failure; layout name-scoped; `validatePathComponent` rejects separators and `.`/`..` at the source. Cleanup is deliberately asynchronous and reclaimable — `discard`/`undiscard`/`removeInBackground`/`sweepDiscarded` quarantine failed removals instead of blocking teardown `[VERIFIED gitworktree/discard.go:35-149]`. Platform-forked removal repair exists because removal keeps failing in the wild (Windows AV, `renv` leaving 0500 dirs). Durable base-ref and prepared-sha facts persisted.

**Review gates (the best in the corpus):**
1. Auto-review coordinator sweeps sessions on an idle threshold with bounded retries.
2. **Head-SHA-fenced feedback delivery** — a `changes_requested` run is only delivered when `DeliveredAt` is nil **and** `currentHeads[run.PRURL] == run.TargetSHA`, "so stale verdicts can never be injected into a coder that has already moved on" `[VERIFIED backend/internal/service/review/review.go:779-793]`.
3. Kanban semantics encode the loop: "auto review's job is to keep re-reviewing this PR until it can approve." Caveat: `changes_requested_same_sha` stops re-reviewing when the SHA hasn't changed — if the coder never pushes, the session wedges in Validating.

**Session harness bridge:** Per-CLI adapter zoo — `claudecode/`, `codex/`, `cursor/`, `copilot/`, `cline/`, `opencode/`, `aider/`, `amp/`, `devin/`, `droid/`, `goose/`, `grok/`, `kimi/`, `kiro/`, `muse/`, plus `fake/`. Claude Code wrapped across `claudecode.go`, `hooks.go`, `continuation.go`, `auth_cache.go`, `terminal_activity.go`. Interface transitions (chat↔TUI) and agent switches are first-class, fault-tested operations.

**Persistence:** SQLite with **158+ numbered migrations**. Event flow is CDC polling (deliberately dependency-free). Usage collection is hook-signal driven with hard bounds (`maxUsageMetadataBytes=256`, `maxCodexSessionMeta=1<<20`, `maxCodexChildIDs=4096`). Pricing is an immutable-snapshot estimator folding provider usage JSON including **cache-write 5m/1h ephemeral splits** `[VERIFIED backend/internal/pricing/runtime.go:447-478]`.

**Major flaws:**
- **No task graph at all** — `DelegateTask` spawns one worker with a prompt string. Parallelism is human-paced; it fundamentally cannot express "B after A" for unattended epics.
- **Silent work drops as a house pattern** — `delegatedTaskTitleConcurrency = 4` with "cosmetic work is dropped at the daemon-wide cap." Fine for titles; will bite applied to real work.
- Auto-review can wedge on a static head (above).
- **Worktree cleanup is the most tortured code in the repo** — platform-forked error classification and permission-repair exist because removal keeps failing.
- `PrepareHostTrustedEnvironment` is a sandbox in name only.
- Presentation races are fixed in the tiebreak rather than at the source (`outranksKanban` exists so the board "never flickers between equally ranked PRs").

**Cherry-pick (high value):** **speculative worktree prepare/claim/cancel token protocol** (`TaskPreparationationToken`, idempotent cancel, `DeletePreparedBranch` only after the worktree is gone) — perfect for any UI needing a workspace before agent config is final; **fact-derived status/Kanban contract** (never persist board columns); **head-SHA-fenced feedback delivery**; **content-addressed reviewer manifest + checkout-free reviewer env**; discard-pile async worktree reclamation; cache-write ephemeral pricing split.

#### agent-swarm — the measured answer to tool-schema bloat
**Philosophy:** "An operating system for AI work" — a lead agent receives goals from Slack/issue trackers/email/API and delegates to workers (Claude Code/Codex/pi/opencode/Devin/ACP) in isolated Docker containers, with shared memory, workflows, schedules, and review gates.

**Orchestration model:** A **dependency-aware task queue with an offer/claim protocol**, plus a separate workflow DAG engine. Task rows carry `dependsOn[]`, `parentTaskId`, `priority` 0–100, and offer fields `offeredTo`/`offeredAt`/`acceptedAt`/`rejectionReason` `[VERIFIED src/types.ts:542-551]`. **Deadlock/stall detection is the most complete in the corpus** — three stall classes: generic `stallThresholdMinutes`, `stallThresholdNoSessionMin` ("tasks with no active session (worker clearly dead)"), `stallThresholdStaleHeartbeatMin`, plus `STEERING_STALL_GRACE_MIN`, `maxAutoAssignPerSweep`, and a **bounded resume budget** `maxResumeGenerations()` with `RESUME_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_REASON` `[VERIFIED src/heartbeat/heartbeat.ts:104-162]`. `codeLevelTriage` expires stale runtime instances and **releases stale offered tasks for offline agents** so offers stuck on dead offerees don't leak. Independently, a queue-stall alarm fires when claimable tasks sit >30min — and its snapshot **excludes tasks with unmet dependencies** ("a worker cannot start them yet") via SQL walking `json_each(COALESCE(queued.dependsOn, '[]'))` `[VERIFIED src/queue-stall-alarm.ts:25-75]`. Deferred wake-ups: `defer-task` wakes on all/any watched task outcome or a deadline.

**Role/tool scoping — THE finding of this audit:** a measured experiment trimmed the external surface to 8 script tools and recorded:
> **full 118 tools ≈ 311 KB (~80K tokens) → scripts-only 8 tools ≈ 8.8 KB (~2.2K tokens), a ~35× cut**
> and: "Claude's ToolSearch already defers schemas but pi/codex/opencode have no tool-search, so for them the full schema really does enter every session."
`[VERIFIED thoughts/shared/research/2026-07-11-scripts-only-mcp-experiment.md; landed as src/utils/scripts-only-mode.ts:11-15, wired at src/http/mcp.ts:202,231]`

This is the empirical grounding for pillar 3 and FV3. It is opt-in (`SCRIPTS_ONLY_MCP`), and the default surface is still ~106–118 tools.

**Worktree/branch isolation:** Isolation is at the **container** boundary (workers in Docker), not a per-session worktree manager. Task rows carry a free-form `dir` — "SHOULD be an absolute path, but the create-task body accepts any string and the DB stores it verbatim" — so **path hygiene is not schema-enforced**.

**Review gates:** Review is a **task-shaped follow-up**, not a hard merge block — "a reviewer task must reach an outcome." Failure reason text `"Blocked dependency"` is matched literally, so review outcomes and dependency blocks share one string-matched channel.

**Session harness bridge:** One adapter per harness (`claude-adapter`, `claude-managed-adapter`, `codex-adapter`+`codex-app-server`, `opencode-adapter`, `pi-mono-adapter`, `devin-adapter`, `acp-adapter`+`acp-targets`, `dsh-adapter`) with per-harness event adaptation into a common swarm-event shape. `harness-version.ts` and `reasoning-effort.ts` normalize cross-harness quirks.

**Persistence:** SQLite with task read model; `dependsOn` round-tripped through `JSON.parse`. Memory is a real subsystem — embeddings, reranker, graph expansion, retrieval store, usefulness stats, and **LLM raters with citation ratings and self-rating**. KV overflow hygiene explicit.

**Major flaws:**
- **`dependsOn` has zero referential integrity** — IDs are arbitrary strings stored verbatim. A typo'd dependency silently never resolves; the queue-stall alarm is the only detector.
- **Path and session binding fields unpinned** (`dir` accepts any string) — a real escape/hygiene risk for containerized workers with shared memory.
- The scripts-only wins are **opt-in** and the observed failure modes were shipped as recommendations (entry-signature confusion, response-envelope guessing, unseeded seed scripts, stale "use ToolSearch" guidance, ~6 round trips per child wait, manual name→id resolution).
- **`MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS=1` deadlocks parent vs auto-review children** — follow-ups queue behind the in-progress parent and the pipeline stalls; fixed in compose config, not the engine.
- Review blocking is string-matched (`t.failureReason?.includes("Blocked dependency")`).

**Cherry-pick (highest leverage in the corpus for pillar 3):** the **code-mode/scripts-only MCP pattern** + its seed-script table (`delegate()`, `wait-for-task()`, `get-child-outputs()`, `swarm-overview()`); **stall taxonomy + resume budget**; **dependency-aware queue-stall SQL**; **offer/claim + stale-offer release**; honest zod row contracts (plain-string IDs with written "why not uuid" notes); **deferred-task wake primitive**.

---

#### opencode-swarm — the gate machinery
**Philosophy:** "Multi-agent systems fail when they're unstructured" — one architect owns all decisions, one task executes at a time, every task is QA'd before the next starts, project state lives in files.

**Orchestration model:** A **gated phase pipeline under a single architect**. Mutation delegations follow "Send, STOP, wait" while **read-only advisory lanes run non-blocking** via `dispatch_lanes_async` returning a `batch_id`, polled via `collect_lane_results` `[VERIFIED src/agents/architect.ts:361]`. That block documents the real failure mode it defends against — oversized inline prompts truncate the tool call and "the lanes never launch" — and prescribes `common_prompt` for shared context. Settled-lane output is delivered **once** (`output_omitted_repeat: true` + `retrieve_lane_output`), preventing re-poll echo. Modes are signal-driven (`[MODE: DEEP_DIVE …]`) and loaded on demand as skills to keep the architect prompt lean.

**Role/tool scoping:** The most rigorous tool-scoping of the six. `AGENT_TOOL_MAP` and `TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS` are **derived** from a compile-checked `TOOL_METADATA` + `TOOL_MANIFEST` pair, superseding hand-maintained maps after the v6.48.0 incident where **six tools were listed but never registered** `[VERIFIED src/config/constants.ts:4-12, docs/engineering-invariants.md]`. Feature-gated per-role maps (`MEMORY_AGENT_TOOL_MAP`, `COUNCIL_AGENT_TOOL_MAP`, `PR_REVIEW_CHILD_AGENT_TOOL_MAP`, …). **Prompt composition accounting** caps architect prompt size at factory exit *and* after sentinel substitution (where user-controlled swarm names enter), truncating tool descriptions in-prompt at a char cap with an ellipsis marker while full descriptions still go through the tools API, emitting `ARCHITECT_PROMPT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` rather than silently dropping mandatory guidance `[VERIFIED docs/architecture.md #2671, src/index.ts:2701]`.

**Worktree/branch isolation:** Real per-lane worktrees (`provisionWorktree`, `removeWorktree`, `checkPathBudget`, `isCleanWorktree`). It **distrusts `git worktree add`'s exit code** — "exiting 0 does not by itself prove" registration — and refuses `git worktree add -f` on missing-on-disk ambiguity `[VERIFIED src/worktree/core.ts:730, 918, issue #2271]`. A **provisional marker covers the gap before `git worktree add`**. Removal is fail-closed: "a blocked or dirty worktree is surfaced, never force-deleted."

**Review gates (the heaviest machinery in the corpus):** `gate-evidence.ts` (1,781 lines) + adversarial evidence-lock tests. **Spec drift is content-hashed** — `computeSpecHash` SHA-256s the effective `.swarm/spec.md` and `isSpecStale` returns typed reasons `[VERIFIED src/utils/spec-hash.ts:9-50]`. PR review has a **bound-commit protocol that fails closed** on wrappers, aliases, force flags, fetch-based local-ref forgery, extra refspecs, and `git -C`; `complete_pr_workflow` requires a clean index and a non-merge direct child of the immutable intake head, verified twice against the remote ref `[VERIFIED src/agents/architect.ts:1161]`. Human-required writes consume a **one-shot session/action/content-bound approval fact** (`WriteApprovalFactV1`) with an issued/consumed ledger and a `WeakSet` of consumed facts, `leastPrivilege`, origins `autonomous|optimizer_proposed|critic_approved|human_approved` `[VERIFIED src/security/write-authority.ts:29-216]`. Scope enforcement throws from `tool.execute.before` — "propagates as tool rejection, NOT as session crash." **Shell writes are statically caught before execution:** `shell-write-detect.ts` (2,459 lines) parses POSIX with `bash-parser` AST and Windows with regex heuristics, covering `WriteCategory = redirect | here_doc | builtin_write | inplace_edit | interpreter_eval | network_download | archive_extract | git_destructive` `[VERIFIED src/hooks/shell-write-detect.ts:35-43]`. The integrity boundary is documented honestly: "Shell classification is a shared bounded tripwire, **never a sandbox**."

**Session harness bridge:** An OpenCode **plugin** — registers `tool: {}`, hooks `tool.execute.before`/`execute`, drives the host's agent loop via architect-emitted tool calls. Tool registration coherence is CI-enforced (`/swarm doctor tools`, registration-adversarial tests). PR/CI integration through hardened `gh`/`glab` resolvers with **honest capability reporting** — GitLab's missing `statusCheckRollup`/`reviewDecision` surface as explicit "unavailable" rather than fabricated values.

**Persistence:** Everything durable under project-root `.swarm/` — `session/state.json`, `epic-state.json`, `spec.md`, `repo-graph.json`. Rehydration is generation-stamped and **deliberately refuses to persist trust-boundary fields** (round-tripping them would make rehydration an attack surface) `[VERIFIED src/state.ts:532-724]`. Containment via `resolveWorkingDirectory` (never `process.cwd()`), `validateProjectRoot` with a depth-20 bounded walk and fail-closed on EPERM/EBUSY. Telemetry is privacy-shaped: "No lesson text and no filesystem paths ever enter the payload."

**Standout innovations:**
- **Shell write detection as static analysis** — nothing else in this survey intercepts `sed -i`, `python -c`, `tar -x`, or `git reset --hard` at the tool boundary.
- **One-shot write-approval fact ledger** — session/action/content-bound, expiring, consumed-once.
- **Spec-hash staleness with typed reasons** — cheap, decisive drift detector.
- **Prompt composition accounting with two-point measurement** (measure *after* user-controlled substitution — the step people miss) and advisory-not-truncate.
- **`docs/engineering-invariants.md`** — a written historical map of every cross-platform bug paid for and the exact invariant each established. **Steal this practice.**
- **Scope leases with cross-process persistence + TTL**, including array-argument scope-bypass handling (`files[]`/`paths[]`/`targetFiles[]`).
- **One-shot lane output delivery** solving the re-poll token-duplication problem for async subagents.

**Major flaws:**
- God files: `src/index.ts` 6,271 lines, `src/state.ts` 4,677.
- Windows write detection is regex-only while POSIX gets a real AST — the weaker path is on the platform where file-locking/AV chaos is worst.
- The tripwire is not a sandbox, by its own admission.
- Recurring bug class: **enumerated lists drifting from registrations** (v6.48.0 phantom tools). The fix was compile-derived metadata, but per-role tool maps are still hand-kept surfaces of the same shape.
- **Grandfathered stale plans** — `isSpecStale` returns `stale: false` for any plan without `specHash`, so pre-feature plans permanently escape drift detection.
- Historical global-state bleed (v6.80.2: module-level `recentToolCalls` shared across sessions → empty `checkpoint: spiral-unknown-xxxx` commits).

**Cherry-pick:** `shell-write-detect.ts` `WriteCategory` taxonomy + bash-parser AST walk; `WriteApprovalFactV1` one-shot approval ledger; spec-hash + typed staleness reasons; prompt-composition budget with two-point measurement; derived `TOOL_METADATA`/`TOOL_MANIFEST` + registration parity tests + `/swarm doctor tools`; fail-closed worktree removal + provisional provisioning marker; one-shot lane output delivery; the engineering-invariants failure-map document format.

**Cross-cutting anti-patterns to design against** (each verified above):
1. **Prompt-text scoping instead of enforcement** (iPolloWork `skillIds`/`pluginIds`) → Studio gates at the MCP gateway.
2. **Decorative DAGs** (iPolloWork `relations` never walked; AO has *no* graph at all) → Studio's DAG is executed by a deterministic scheduler or it does not ship.
3. **Fixed per-turn injection tax** (claude-smart's ~150–250 token citation instruction on every Edit/Write/Bash) → Studio's Tool Lens budgets every injected byte.
4. **Coordination on the hot path** (munder-difflin's synchronous `git commit` per message) → Studio's plane writes ledger rows (cheap) and commits deliberately.
5. **Un-incremented loop guards** (munder-difflin `HOP_CAP`) → every counter in Studio is unit-tested to actually increment.
6. **Unbounded append-only files** (`cost-ledger.jsonl`, `.sent/` kept forever) → Studio's ledger is a SQLite table with retention; receipts are content-addressed.
7. **Enumerated lists drifting from registrations** (opencode-swarm v6.48.0 six phantom tools) → Studio derives tool maps from a compile-checked manifest and runs registration parity tests.
8. **God modules** (Orkas `bus.ts` 10,751 lines; paseo `agent-manager.ts` 5,363; opencode-swarm `index.ts` 6,271) → Studio's plane is composed of small modules with documented lock order.
9. **Best-effort disk hygiene** (AoE "cosmetic leak" comment; AO's tortured removal repair) → Studio's worktree teardown is fail-closed + trash-rename + ledger-reconciled orphans.
10. **String-matched control flow** (agent-swarm `failureReason?.includes("Blocked dependency")`) → Studio uses typed outcome enums.
